subject: Signature sequencing & change order for capacity uplift
messages:
From: Alicia Park <a.park@helioai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity uplift request + proposed ordering path

Jordan —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our internal planning, we need to add an incremental 120 GPU nodes across two phases (80 in Sept, 40 in Nov). I attached our updated order form (hl-orderform_v2.pdf) with the breakdown and the requested start dates.

We tried to reflect the pricing band you quoted on the call, but procurement wants the redline and the signatory order documented before they circulate internally. Can Redwood confirm:
- the change order number you will use (so we can reference it in our PO)
- whether you require HelioAI Finance or VP Eng to sign first for our internal approval flow
- any proration rules for Sept start if the prod go-live is mid-month

We'd like to turn this around quickly — ideally signed within 7 business days.

Thanks,
Alicia Park
Head of Procurement, HelioAI
Alicia Park | HelioAI

Attachment: hl-orderform_v2.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <a.park@helioai.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift request + proposed ordering path

Alicia —

Appreciate the clear order form. Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Marissa (Sales Ops) so we can get a coordinated redline and a signature routing. Quick answers up front: we will assign a change-order ID (CO-HL-1789) and we typically ask the purchasing/legal approver at the customer to sign first, followed by the customer exec (VP Eng) if you require technical acceptance, then Redwood executes via DocuSign. We can, however, flip that sequence if HelioAI has a strict PO-first policy — Kimberly, see notes below.

Kimberly — attached is the order form from Helio. Can you review for: billing proration clause, SLA uplift for added capacity, and the SOW language that defines "burst" vs "reserved" capacity? I'm including a draft redline stub (JR_redline_20260729.docx) for your edits.

Marissa — can you prepare the procurement checklist and the DocuSign envelope template and confirm our signing name and countersignatory?

I'll assemble a short MAP (mutual action plan) once we have legal comments.

—Jordan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: JR_redline_20260729.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alicia Park <a.park@helioai.com>
Date: 2026-07-30T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift request + proposed ordering path — initial legal redline

Jordan / Alicia / Marissa —

I reviewed the order form and added comments in JR_redline_20260729.docx. High-level items:

1) Billing/proration: propose explicit language "Charges for increases in reserved capacity shall be prorated based on the effective date of the change order and invoiced in the next billing cycle; any mid-month provisioning that results in partial-month usage shall be billed at a daily pro rata rate." Helio, please let us know if you need a fixed invoice trigger instead.

2) SLA & performance: for the added nodes we will maintain existing SLA terms; however, for burst pool behavior we need to define expected QoS. I added a sentence to the SOW requiring a 95th percentile latency target for production traffic associated with the uplifted capacity.

3) Termination/rollback: added a 30-day notice window for de-provisioning of added nodes to avoid orphaned billing/spikes.

4) Price floor: given the size of the uplift, recommend a short-term volume discount but with a minimum per-node fee to protect both sides. See redline.

I am ok with the proposed signatory sequencing (Procurement -> Exec -> Redwood) as long as HelioAI's PO issuance does not itself modify commercial terms. If Helio insists on Finance-first signing, we can mark the change order as "PO contingent".

I'll stand by for Marissa's DocuSign workflow.

- Kimberly
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: JR_redline_20260729.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <a.park@helioai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-31T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift request + proposed ordering path — signature routing & checklist

Hi all —

Thanks — I put together a procurement_checklist.xlsx and a suggested signature sequence:
- Step 1: HelioAI Procurement (Alicia) signs CO-HL-1789 to confirm commercial terms and effective dates.
- Step 2: HelioAI VP Eng (Victor Chen) signs (technical acceptance) if HelioAI requires engineering sign-off — this can be a separate sign-off field on the same DocuSign envelope.
- Step 3: Redwood countersigns (authorized signatory: Marissa Cole, Head of Sales Ops).

DocuSign envelope prepared: https://docusign.net/abc123 — I will add the procurement_checklist.xlsx to the envelope as an attachment and attach the JR_redline_20260729.docx as the working redline.

Invoice trigger: Marissa recommends "effective date" triggers invoice on the next billing cycle; if HelioAI prefers "provisioning complete" we can change.

I've attached the checklist and a short notes tab that lists required fields for the PO. Please review and confirm and I will send the envelope.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: procurement_checklist.xlsx

From: Alicia Park <a.park@helioai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Victor Chen <v.chen@helioai.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift request + proposed ordering path — approval and timing

Marissa / Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement is aligned with the proposed signatory order (Procurement -> VP Eng -> Redwood). We do need the following spelled out in the change order before we sign:
- explicit transition schedule (date windows for Sept and Nov provisioning)
- invoice trigger: HelioAI will accept "effective date" but needs a clear provisioning acceptance metric (e.g., nodes available in production and health check passing for 48 hours)
- confirmation of proration language (Kimberly's wording sounds acceptable; prefer invoice on next billing cycle).

We can commit to signing within 5 business days after we receive the revised redline with the transition schedule included. Once we sign we'll issue a PO referencing CO-HL-1789.

Best,
Alicia Park
Head of Procurement, HelioAI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <a.park@helioai.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Victor Chen <v.chen@helioai.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift request + proposed ordering path — final next steps

Alicia / team —

Thanks — summary and next steps:
1) Kimberly will incorporate the transition windows (Sept 10–15 for 80 nodes; Nov 8–12 for 40 nodes) and preserve the proration language (invoice on next billing cycle; 48-hour health-check acceptance).
2) Marissa will update the DocuSign envelope (CO-HL-1789), attach the checklist and redline, and set signing order (Procurement -> VP Eng -> Redwood). DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/abc123.
3) Helio commits to sign within 5 business days of receipt; Helio will issue PO referencing CO-HL-1789 after signature.
4) Redwood will schedule provisioning windows with Ops once fully executed.

I'll circulate the updated redline and the MAP by EOD tomorrow. If that timing doesn't work for Helio, let me know and we'll expedite.

—Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: JR_redline_20260729.docx, procurement_checklist.xlsx, hl-orderform_v2.pdf
